answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting work, whether it writes a sonnet, sources walnut timber, or computes a graph vertex cover. Creating identities is cheap, but operating 1,000 eligible sellers ties up $100,000 for a month. Splitting into more accounts therefore adds no free capacity: each extra active identity requires another bond, imposing a proportional capital cost on a sybil attacker.
